readback.body:
🤖 **Comment from Codex working with Leo:** **Decision [D018, revision 1](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d018): the backend must represent randomization through the existing `doLog` field.** Thanks, Aaron — agreed that a completed experiment can still randomize. We’re keeping allocations that randomize subject to opt-out, including ordinary percentage splits and partial enrollment. The backend owns that classification; evaluators retain the existing `doLog` predicate and future-mode cutoff rule. This records Leo’s clarification in [this decision thread](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368#discussion_r4343813763); the earlier withdrawn selection remains in [provenance](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/local-decision.json). **Implemented in [d0a2de5b58](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/d0a2de5b58dba158941d2c2f81016276a45ea2c1); validated after merging main at [0ae33d8f11](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/0ae33d8f112685502bb8f16d8c96efbecb70219b).** The compiler sets `doLog=true` when shard selection changes the variation or match/fallthrough outcome. Deterministic completed winners remain `false`, while existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, and holdout logging requirements are preserved. **Shared proofs:** [draft FFE test-data PR #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55) contains the [D018 decision](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d018), its Lean proofs, and the linked validation history.
Behavior — the distinction we are preserving | Allocation | Compiler output | Immediate mode with a valid subject cutoff | | --- | --- | --- | | Completed experiment still splitting 50/50 | `doLog=true` | Skip the allocation. | | Ordinary percentage split | `doLog=true` | Skip the allocation. | | Single variant with partial percentage enrollment | `doLog=true` | Skip the allocation. | | Deterministic completed ordinary winner | `doLog=false` | Remains eligible for delivery. | | Existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, or generated-holdout logging | Preserve the existing logging requirement. | Skip when `doLog=true`. | This deliberately enables exposure logging for ordinary randomized allocations. Targeting rules and time windows do not themselves make an allocation random; changing between match and fallthrough does. First-match order, unreachable variants, empty ranges, and same-variant coverage are handled by the native classifier. Future mode keeps its strictly-before cutoff rule: earlier activation remains eligible, while unknown activation is conservatively excluded. Deployment still requires the fallback-preserving child, regenerated UFCs, and activation coverage for newly logging allocations.
Native validation — local checks at 0ae33d8f11 - **918 compiler tests, 283 database repository tests, and 275 runner/primary-analysis tests pass.** The [merged-source receipt](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/main-merge-native-validation.json) records the commands, source hashes, and exact execution scope. The repository run preceded only the compiler-test snapshot/comment correction; its library source was unchanged. - The classifier matches **500 independent raw-bucket enumeration cases**, alongside targeted cases for partial enrollment, first-match ordering, unreachable variants, and same-variant coverage. - Before main integration, restoring the old `doLog` output failed the completed 50/50, ordinary 50/50, and partial-enrollment regressions. The [negative-control receipt](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/native-validation.json) retains its original source and patch pins; restoring the fix passed both Go suites uncached. - Main introduced a golden snapshot with seven old `doLog=false` expectations. That initial failure is preserved in [V052](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#v052). Updating only those seven logging bits leaves **every assignment field unchanged**; the subsequent compiler run passes, recorded in [V053](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#v053). These are local native checks. The model proof does not establish correctness of the Go partition classifier. Child-stack integration, CI, and deployed behavior remain separate evidence.
Sneak preview — turning review decisions into reusable, checked contracts The shared decisions and proofs are published in **[draft FFE test-data PR #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55)** at [99854cf878](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/commit/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34): 1. **[A versioned English decision — D018, revision 1](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d018)**, linked to where it was set. 2. **[An executable Lean model and checked proofs](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/lean/BackendReview.lean#L6-L41)** of the producer/evaluator composition. 3. **[The existing semantic corpus](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/corpus/browser-proposal.jsonl)** and **[operational corpus](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/corpus/inactive-path.jsonl)**, preserving the broader opt-out contract. These are not new D018 producer-classification cases; the classifier has separate native enumeration and regression tests. 4. **[A linked history of evidence](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#historical-linked-checks)**, preserving passing and failing checks separately from the decision’s authority. For example, [this theorem](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/lean/BackendReview.lean#L26-L28) is checked in the published model: ```lean theorem immediate_excludes_randomized_allocations (existingExposure : Bool) : (compiledPolicy .immediate .valid .missing existingExposure true).exclude = true := by cases existingExposure <;> rfl ``` In plain English: within this model, an allocation classified as randomized is excluded in immediate mode with a valid subject cutoff, even without an existing exposure-logging requirement. The modeled compiler combines the two requirements as `existingExposure || randomized`; it does not infer randomization from native shard data. The [model validation](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/model-validation.json) passes **53 theorem audits**, including seven new D018 theorems, plus **313 existing semantic cases and 36 operational cases**. A separate theorem distinguishes the old non-logging split from the corrected producer contract. The useful result is a reviewable rule with a source-pinned evidence trail. The Lean proof establishes properties of the model; the [native receipt](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/99854cf87802e03d2cc2c5ed324dfabcaafc5f34/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/main-merge-native-validation.json) establishes the bounded compiler checks above. The central PR remains a draft, and fleet adoption remains a separate decision.
